about.title: Simi Valley Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Simi Valley walk out of a clinic or hospital better than they walked in. Sometimes, though, a missed diagnosis, a surgical slip, or a medication mix-up leaves a Ventura County family dealing with harm that competent care would have avoided. That gap between what a careful provider should have done and what actually happened is the heart of a malpractice claim under California law. A disappointing result on its own is not enough; the question is whether the standard of care was breached and whether that breach caused the injury. Answering it almost always takes a qualified medical expert, and California's MICRA rules add tight deadlines, a 90-day pre-suit notice, and a cap on non-economic damages that adjusts upward each year. We handle medical malpractice claims on contingency, so you owe no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Simi Valley Residents Choose Us

items.title: MICRA Deadlines Are Short
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discovered the injury, and never more than three years from when it occurred. Reaching out early leaves room for the 90-day pre-suit notice and a proper record review.

items.title: Expert-Backed Case Evaluation

items.title: Free Consultation, Contingency-Based Representation
items.desc: We charge you nothing for your initial review, and we handle cases on contingency. If there is no recovery, there is no attorney fee.

items.question: I was treated after a crash on SR-118 and my condition got worse. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: Not automatically. Injuries from collisions on the Ronald Reagan Freeway or Los Angeles Avenue can worsen even with excellent treatment. Malpractice requires proof that a provider fell below the accepted standard of care and that the lapse caused additional harm, which is why we will usually have a medical expert examine your records.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Ventura County?
items.answer: Under MICRA, the general rule is one year from the date you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and no more than three years from the date the injury happened. You also must give the provider 90 days' written notice before filing suit. Because these windows overlap, it is wise to contact us as soon as you suspect something went wrong.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: Yes. California caps non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases, and that cap rises each year under current law. Economic losses such as medical bills and lost wages are handled separately. We can explain how the current figures apply to your situation.
